description_full: Torex Resources Inc., a precious metals mining company, engages in the acquisition, exploration, and development of mineral properties in Mexico and the United States. The company explores gold, copper, silver, and carbon deposits. Its flagship project is a 100% owned Morelos Complex covering an area of 29,000 hectares located in Guerrero, Mexico. Torex Resources Inc. was formerly known as Torex Gold Resources Inc. and changed its name to Torex Resources Inc. in October 2026. Torex Resources Inc. was incorporated in 1980 and is based in Toronto, Canada.

financial_summary: Torex Gold Resources Inc. is a mid-cap basic materials business with a $4.2B market cap on $1.3B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +15% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +3.2pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 19% against a 9% cost of capital — a 10-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 38%.

The business throws off $135M in free cash flow — roughly 10 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.21× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.0× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage of 74× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield is only 1.0%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 3.1× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
